//: Copy this file to cdk.json and fill in the values. cdk.json itself is gitignored: the app half of it holds real secrets (see infra/.gitignore and CLAUDE_problems.md P046). This example exists so that a fresh clone can run cdk at all -- cdk.json is also what tells the CDK CLI where the app entrypoint is, so without one, even `npx cdk synth` fails before reaching any of this project's code.

context.//bootstrapQualifier: Deploys through the scoped tool0001 bootstrap, the same one the sibling SmomaSite/SmomaMail stacks use. The account default bootstrap (hnb659fds) runs as AdministratorAccess and is denied to this user. Do not change this.
context.//: ----- everything below is yours to set -----
context.//account: The AWS account, written down rather than inherited from whichever profile is active.
context.//region: Where the Lambda lives. The domain stack is always us-east-1 regardless, because CloudFront certificates have to be.
context.//flaskSecretKey: Signs the Flask session cookie. Generate with: python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))". Use a different value than your local .env. REAL SECRET -- never commit.
context.//googleCredentialsJson: The Google service-account key, full JSON as downloaded, collapsed to one line. Same value as your local .env's GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS_JSON. REAL SECRET -- never commit.
context.//googleSheetId: The target Google Sheet ID. Same value as your local .env's GOOGLE_SHEET_ID. Not a secret, but it goes here with the others.
context.//memoryMb: Lambda memory. Empty means the default, 512.
context.//timeoutSeconds: Lambda timeout. Empty means the default, 15.
context.//appStackNote: Leave flaskSecretKey/googleCredentialsJson/googleSheetId empty and PmtcApp is not created at all -- which is the point: the domain stack below can then be deployed from a machine that has none of the app's secrets, with no way to redeploy the live Lambda by accident.
context.//domain: The subdomain the tool answers to. Hostname characters only -- letters, digits, hyphens. An underscore is rejected by both ACM and CloudFront.
context.//certArn: An issued us-east-1 certificate for that domain, requested standalone with `aws acm request-certificate` rather than by CloudFormation. See domain-stack.ts for why.
context.//functionUrl: The deployed PmtcApp stack's own AppUrl output, pasted in verbatim. Not a cross-stack reference, on purpose -- see bin/app.ts.
context.//domainStackNote: domain, certArn and functionUrl go together: set all three, or none. Setting some but not all fails at synth by design.
context.//mailNote: ----- report delivery (PmtcMail). None of these is a secret, so unlike the app block above, the real values live here in the committed example rather than only in a local cdk.json. -----
context.//mailDomain: The verified SES domain the report is sent from, and the switch that creates PmtcMail at all. Leave it empty and the stack is not in the app. NOTE: this stack does not verify the domain and must not -- geniusdrive.com is already verified in this account and is owned by the sibling SmomaMail stack. See mail-stack.ts.
context.//sender: The From address. Needs no mailbox: SES verifies the domain, never the mailbox. Empty means reports@<mailDomain>.
context.//replyTo: Where a reply to the report actually goes. Must be a real mailbox. Points at Genius Drive rather than K1x because until the tool is live every send is a test, and a test reply should not land on the client. Re-pointing it is a go-live step.
context.//notify: Where SES bounce and complaint notices go. AWS emails this address once to confirm the SNS subscription; until somebody clicks it, the topic notifies nobody.
context.//bcc: Who is blind-copied on every report, comma-separated. Set 2026-08-31 per Ben/K1x: tiana.maher@k1x.io, scott.turner@k1x.io. It lives here rather than as a deploy-script argument on purpose -- the copy is blind, so a deploy that dropped it would look completely normal and nobody would notice until the reader asked why reports had stopped.
